subject: Request: billing slab parity + onboarding concession — Elara Health
messages:
From: Emma Lawson <emma@elarahealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: billing slab parity + onboarding concession

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile and the routing/fallback story. We have one commercial ask from procurement before we circle back to our CFO: can Redwood match slab pricing parity with a competitor we're evaluating (they've offered a steeper step-down on per-token price at volume tiers) and provide a one-time onboarding credit to offset integration costs?

Specifically:
- Parity on the tiered unit price at the 10M+ token slab for year one.
- A one-time onboarding credit of $40k tied to professional services against the initial invoice.

We're close on contract language (attached a short usage forecast) but procurement has indicated we need VP/CFO level confirmation for any deviation from standard public rates.

Emma
Emma Lawson
Head of Product Partnerships | Elara Health
emma@elarahealth.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachment: usage_forecast_elara.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: billing slab parity + onboarding concession

Marissa / Jordan — forwarding Elara's procurement note. High strategic fit: healthcare analytics, potential multi-year expansion. Quick summary and my call:

Why this matters
- Elara is forecasting 18–24M tokens per month after Q2 2027 per the attached forecast, potential ARR ~ $2.1M in year one if ramp hits.
- Competitor has offered a steep step-down at 10M slab; procurement is pushing for parity plus $40k onboarding credit.

Risks of saying no
- Likely move to competitor given integration timeline and negotiating leverage.
- We risk losing not just direct spend but referral opportunities into payer customers.

Proposed concession (recommended)
- One-time onboarding credit: $30k (compromise vs their $40k ask).
- Temporary slab parity for year one only: match competitor unit price at 10M+ slab but require a 12-month minimum committed usage (ramp metrics to be defined).
- Protective clauses: phased rollback to our standard published rates at month 13 if commit is not met; usage audit clause.

Can you and Jordan review margin impact and advise if this can be approved at VP/CFO level? If not, what's the minimum structure that would placate procurement without opening the floodgates?

Attachments: usage_forecast_elara.xlsx

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwoodinference.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: billing slab parity + onboarding concession

On Wed, Dec 1, 2026 at 9:04 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Marissa / Jordan — forwarding Elara's procurement note. High strategic fit: healthcare analytics, potential multi-year expansion. Quick summary and my call:

Agree with Naomi's recommendation — here's the commercial justification from GTM:

Business case
- Elara is an ideal reference for health analytics buyers (strong case studies, active conversations w/ two enterprise payer customers).
- They have an internal timeline: deploy POC Jan–Feb, production Q2. If we stall pricing now, procurement timelines push to Q3 and risk competitor adoption.

Recommended ask to VP/CFO
- Approve a $30k one-time onboarding credit.
- Approve temporary slab parity for Year 1 only, conditioned on: 12-month minimum commitment of $1.8M ARR equivalent and a clause to revert to standard published pricing at month 13 unless thresholds met.
- Request legal to accept a short audit & ramp schedule instead of open-ended credits.

Mitigations
- Cap total projected concession to $120k NRR impact in year one (this includes onboarding credit + estimated gross margin delta from slab parity).
- Attach an upsell protection: if Elara expands to additional product modules, revert to our standard uplift pricing on those modules.

If Jordan is comfortable with the margin model under these constraints, I recommend we bring this to VP/CFO for sign-off this week.

Marissa Cole
VP Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

Attachment referenced: Elara_MA_v3_redlines.pdf (contract redlines)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: billing slab parity + onboarding concession

Naomi / Marissa — thanks for the clear case. A few finance asks before we escalate: 

Numbers/constraints I need to sign off:
- Confirmed modelled revenue and gross margin impact attached (see note). With a $30k onboarding credit + year-one slab parity, our model shows a ~14% gross margin decrease on incremental usage in year one (assuming ramp in attached forecast).
- Suggest a hard cap: concession accounting treatment should cap cumulative credit+discount exposure at $120k NPV (matches Marissa's cap). If Elara breaches ramp, credits should reverse per contract.
- Propose a ramp KPI schedule: 0–3 months: POC; months 4–6: 40% of target; months 7–12: 100% of committed usage. Failure to hit month 12 target triggers rollback.

I can support VP/CFO approval if legal accepts the rollback mechanics, we document the cap in the contract (schedule), and sales adds the minimum commitment with clawback language.

Please prepare a one-page executive memo summarizing ask, net present value impact, and the proposed contractual guardrails — that is what CFO prefers for sign-off.

Jordan Blake
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwoodinference.com>, VP Finance <vpfinance@redwoodinference.com>, CFO <cfo@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: EXEC MEMO: Elara Health — request for VP/CFO signoff on slab parity + onboarding credit (DL-73819)

VP Finance / CFO — requesting expedited approval for a limited concession to close Elara Health. Summary below; full materials attached.

Executive summary
- Ask: Approve $30k one-time onboarding credit + temporary parity on 10M+ token slab for Year 1 only. Conditions: 12-month minimum committed usage of $1.8M ARR-equivalent and contract schedule with ramp KPIs and rollback clause.
- Strategic rationale: Elara is a high-visibility healthcare analytics customer; expected to be an important reference and has potential upsell into payer integrations. Closing now accelerates revenue recognition into FY27 and improves our position in healthcare vertical.
- Financial guardrails: Jordan has modelled the impact — expected ~14% gross margin reduction on incremental usage in Y1 but cumulative concession is capped at $120k NPV. Clawback/rollback language to be enforced if ramp not met.

Attachments (for signoff)
- Elara_MA_v3_redlines.pdf (contract redlines with rollback & cap schedule)
- usage_forecast_elara.xlsx (sales forecast & model)
- One-page memo (attached below in the DocuSign link)

Decision requested
- VP Finance / CFO sign-off to proceed with the negotiated concession as summarized. If approved, legal will finalize redlines and I will send the signature packet (DocuSign link included).

If you prefer, I can present this in a 10-minute sync — otherwise please reply with your approval or questions.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Elara_MA_v3_redlines.pdf; usage_forecast_elara.xlsx
